'''Nicole Tomczak-Jaegermann''' [[Royal Society of Canada|FRSC]] (8 June 1945 – 17 June 2022) was a [[Polish Canadians|Polish-Canadian]] [[mathematician]], a professor of mathematics at the [[University of Alberta]], and the holder of the [[Canada Research Chair]] in Geometric Analysis.<ref name="crc">[http://www.chairs-chaires.gc.ca/chairholders-titulaires/profile-eng.aspx?profileId=545 Canada Research Chair in Geometric Analysis], retrieved 3 December 2010.</ref>

==Contributions==

Her research is in [[Geometric analysis|geometric]] [[functional analysis]],<ref name="crc"/> and is unusual in combining [[asymptotic analysis]] with the theory of [[Banach space]]s and infinite-dimensional [[convex body|convex bodies]]. It formed a key component of [[Fields Medal|Fields medal]]ist [[Timothy Gowers]]' solution to [[Stefan Banach]]'s homogeneous space problem, posed in 1932.<ref name="fields">[http://www.fields.utoronto.ca/press/05-06/tomczak-jaegermann.html Tomczak-Jaegermann wins 2006 CRM-Fields-PIMS prize], [[Fields Institute]], accessed 3 December 2010.</ref> Her 1989 monograph on [[Banach–Mazur compactum|Banach–Mazur distances]] is also highly cited.<ref>{{citation
| last = Tomczak-Jaegermann
| first = Nicole
| title = Banach-Mazur distances and finite-dimensional operator ideals
| series = Pitman Monographs and Surveys in Pure and Applied Mathematics 38
| publisher = Longman Scientific & Technical, Harlow; copublished in the United States with John Wiley & Sons, Inc., New York
| year = 1989
| pages = xii+395
| isbn = 0-582-01374-7|mr=0993774}}.</ref>

==Education and career==
Tomczak-Jaegermann earned her M.S. in 1968 from the [[University of Warsaw]],<ref name="fields"/> and her Ph.D. from the same university in 1974, under the supervision of [[Aleksander Pełczyński]].<ref>{{mathgenealogy|name=Nicole Tomczak-Jaegermann|id=44781}}.</ref> She remained on the faculty at the University of Warsaw from 1975 until 1983, when she moved to Alberta.<ref name="fields"/>

==Recognition==
In 1996, Tomczak-Jaegermann was elected to the [[Royal Society of Canada]],<ref>[http://www.rsc.ca/ RSC], accessed 3 December 2010.</ref> and in 1999 she won the [[Krieger–Nelson Prize]] for an outstanding female Canadian mathematician.<ref name="fields"/> In 1998 she was an Invited Speaker of the [[International Congress of Mathematicians]] in Berlin.<ref>{{cite book|author=Tomczak-Jaegermann, Nicole|chapter=From finite to infinite-dimensional phenomena in geometric functional analysis on local and asymptotic levels|title=Doc. Math. (Bielefeld) Extra Vol. ICM Berlin, 1998, vol. II|year=1998|pages=731–742|chapter-url=https://www.elibm.org/ft/10011685000}}</ref> She was the winner of the 2006 [[CRM-Fields-PIMS prize]] for exceptional research in mathematics.<ref name="fields"/>

==Death==
Tomczak-Jaegermann died on 17 June 2022 at the age 77 in [[Edmonton, Alberta]], Canada.<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.ptm.org.pl/zawartosc/zmar%C5%82-nicole-tomczak-jaegermann-1945-2022 |title=Zmarła Nicole Tomczak-Jaegermann (1945–2022) |access-date=27 June 2022 |archive-date=8 July 2022 |archive-url=https://archive.today/20220708101225/https://www.ptm.org.pl/zawartosc/zmar%C5%82-nicole-tomczak-jaegermann-1945-2022 |url-status=dead }}</ref>
